searchText: consensus layer call in just over 2 hours https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/429 Reminder, the first ~45 minutes will be used for Kintsugi 🍵 office hours and we invite both CL and EL teams to join i'll post a zoom link just before stream: https://youtu.be/1fIg_t6hZ8U actually i think we will use the long-standing zoom link so if you need it dm me so i can share and minimize any zoom bombing Hey I apologize for the newbie question, but I am trying to put out a PR for the specs. I see this in `specs/altair/beacon-chain.md:` ``` process_operations(state, block.body) # [Modified in Altair] ``` What is that modification? or what is that reference for? just to call out for readers that one object in the call graph has changed for altair in this case, the state, the block's body and the functionality inside `process_operations` as it is a core driver Quick call notes: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/S1trJ8UFK I'm a bit surprised, so any function that has its arguments changed has to be marked? `process_operations` itself didn't change in Altair. And the changes in `state` and `block.body` do not affect the functioning of `process_operations` do they? so in this case it is to call attention that the top-level `process_block` changed in altair with the new `process_attestation` and `process_deposit` feel free to open a PR w/ out the comments and i'm sure they can get added as needed Thanks, I didn't get this particular one so mine may be following a different pattern that the spec 🙂 Icymi, I've fully updated (and almost finished) my annotated spec for Altair: https://upgrading-ethereum.info/altair/annotated-spec. (Also available at https://eth2book.info/altair/annotated-spec just to trigger certain individuals.) Some rough edges that I'll work on in due course, but hopefully useful to some of my fellow protocol nerds. > just to trigger certain individuals. <@!573787335796326400> Is that a dare? /jk. "eth2" is fine here, I'm happy if it's used for the evolution of ethereum rather than the consensus-only part. Yep, that's exactly my position too. But it seems to regularly upset a bunch of people (scroll back a few messages for an instance.) The problem with the name is that it causes confusion to newbies who then go out looking for where to buy eth2 coins and they get scammed. It isn't that it isn't specific enough for technical discussion (though also true, that isn't my primary concern). Sorry for the continued questions, why does `get_validator_from_deposit` take a `BeaconState` as argument? it does not seem to be used probably a hold over from an earlier time when it did use the state care to make a PR cleaning it up? just note we need to be extra careful changing the phase 0 specs luckily this one does not affect any other fork if you want bonus points, it would be great to lint the pyspec and see if we can find anything else w/ unused arguments -- i would expect there is some python tooling for this I think I just messed up and put the argument in there https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/commit/1623086088e6f0496566ab7d50d16a8c78cdebf0 would be good for our linter to pick up unused args I thought it did, tbh it is a very common pattern 🙂 Can do that eventually, now I'm wasting a couple of afternoons in putting up a PR that will be quickly dismissed 🙂 (in the spec) you can derisk the process by chatting about it here or in the appropriate channel? may be easier to get quick text feedback first if the PR is big or involved yeah that's why I know it'll be bombed

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Hey I apologize for the newbie question, but I am trying to put out a PR for the specs. I see this in `specs/altair/beacon-chain.md:`
```
process_operations(state, block.body) # [Modified in Altair]
```
What is that modification? or what is that reference for?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: just to call out for readers that one object in the call graph has changed for altair

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: in this case, the state, the block's body and the functionality inside `process_operations` as it is a core driver

excerpts.author: benjaminion
excerpts.content: Quick call notes: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/S1trJ8UFK

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I'm a bit surprised, so any function that has its arguments changed has to be marked? `process_operations` itself didn't change in Altair. And the changes in `state` and `block.body` do not affect the functioning of `process_operations` do they?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: so in this case it is to call attention that the top-level `process_block` changed in altair

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: with the new `process_attestation` and `process_deposit`

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: feel free to open a PR w/ out the comments and i'm sure they can get added as needed

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Thanks, I didn't get this particular one so mine may be following a different pattern that the spec 🙂

excerpts.author: benjaminion
excerpts.content: Icymi, I've fully updated (and almost finished) my annotated spec for Altair: https://upgrading-ethereum.info/altair/annotated-spec. (Also available at https://eth2book.info/altair/annotated-spec just to trigger certain individuals.) Some rough edges that I'll work on in due course, but hopefully useful to some of my fellow protocol nerds.
